rule.body: The verb must agree with its subject in number. A singular subject takes a singular verb (is, was, has, goes); a plural subject takes a plural verb (are, were, have, go). Find the real subject first and ignore any words between it and the verb. 'Each', 'every', 'everyone' and 'one of the + plural noun' are singular. After 'there', the verb agrees with the noun that comes after it.
rule.example: One of the boys in our class has won the prize.

questions.stem: The girls in the choir ___ beautifully every Sunday.
questions.explanation: The subject is 'The girls', which is plural, so it takes the plural verb 'sing'.

questions.stem: Every student ___ to wear the school badge.
questions.explanation: 'Every student' means each single student, so it takes a singular verb: 'is expected'.

questions.stem: There ___ three oranges on the table.
questions.explanation: After 'there', the verb agrees with the noun that follows. 'Three oranges' is plural, so we use 'are'.

questions.stem: My brother ___ to school by bus every morning.
questions.explanation: 'My brother' is one person, and 'every morning' shows a habit, so we use the singular present form 'goes'.

questions.stem: One of the boys ___ lost his bag on the way to school.
questions.explanation: The subject is 'One', not 'boys'. 'One' is singular, so the verb is 'has'.

questions.stem: The box of pencils ___ on the shelf.
questions.explanation: The subject is 'The box', which is singular. 'of pencils' only describes it, so the verb is 'is'.

questions.stem: Everyone in the hall ___ standing when the principal walked in.
questions.explanation: 'Everyone' is singular, and the action is in the past ('walked in'), so the verb is 'was'.

questions.stem: Each of the candidates ___ given an answer sheet before the paper started.
questions.explanation: The subject is 'Each', which is singular, and the time is past, so the verb is 'was'.

questions.stem: The results of the examination, which was written in May, ___ been released.
questions.explanation: The main subject is 'The results', which is plural. The clause about the examination does not change it, so the verb is 'have'.

questions.stem: There ___ been many complaints about the noise since the new shop opened.
questions.explanation: The verb agrees with 'many complaints', which is plural, and 'since' calls for the present perfect, so we use 'have been'.
